**(a)** The phenomenon is **resonance**. When the stem of the vibrating tuning fork is placed on the sound box, the box and the wire are set into forced vibration at 300 Hz. If the natural frequency of the wire equals the frequency of the fork, the wire vibrates with a very large amplitude: this is resonance. The paper rider on wire B falls off because wire B is in resonance, its natural frequency being 300 Hz. Wire A has a different natural frequency, so it vibrates only with a small amplitude (forced vibration) and the rider stays on.

**(b)** **f is less than 300 Hz.** The natural frequency of a stretched wire is

\(f = \dfrac{1}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}}\)

where \(m\) is the mass per unit length. Both wires have the same material, the same length \(l\) and the same tension (10 kgf), but wire A is thicker, so its mass per unit length is greater. A larger \(m\) gives a lower frequency. Since B (thinner) resonates at 300 Hz, the thicker wire A has a natural frequency \(f\) less than 300 Hz.

Applying Fleming's left hand rule (forefinger down along the field, middle finger from P to Q along the current), the thumb points to the left, towards **C**. So the rod moves towards C.

**(b)** **Fleming's left hand rule.** Stretch the forefinger, middle finger and thumb of the left hand mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points along the magnetic field and the middle finger along the current, the thumb gives the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor.

**(c)** The force experienced by the rod **increases**.

**(d)** The force on the rod is \(F = BIl\). The resistance of the rod is \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\); a rod of the same material and length but greater cross-sectional area \(A\) has a smaller resistance. With the same cell, a larger current \(I\) flows through it, so the force \(BIl\) becomes larger.
answers.flag: (a) depends on reading the perspective drawing: rails taken as lying in a horizontal plane (lower rail = nearer), rod P near, Q far, cell's long plate (+) on the lower/near rail. That gives current P to Q, field downward, force towards C, so True.
